changes.current_line: Financial infrastructure to grow globally, in every currency.
changes.change: For domestic subscription businesses (e.g. multi-studio fitness), don't open with the global line. Open with an offer on their own data: "Send us one month of your failed renewals and we'll show you which ones usually come back with a retry or an updated card. Your file, not our average."
changes.why: The global opener met silence at a US-plus-a-few-Canadian-studios business, while the analysis Tobi ran on Corelane's own failed renewals is what landed.

changes.current_line: Recover failed payments automatically with smart retries.
changes.change: For subscription and membership businesses, frame recovery as churn the board already tracks: "Part of your churn is members who never meant to leave. Their card just failed. Win them back automatically."
changes.why: The buyer's problem was a board-reported churn number, and recovery only became the topic once churn was split into cancellations and failed cards. The customer's phrase "members who never meant to leave" is sharper than "failed payments."

changes.current_line: Online and in-store on one platform; the line between them has pretty much disappeared.
changes.change: For businesses with front desks running on studio or vertical software, retire "unified commerce" and the one-platform claim. Say: "Online membership billing now; front desk through our partner integration." Describe the front-desk workflow (one screen to check a member in and sell a water bottle) only where it can be demoed live inside the prospect's own software.
changes.why: "Unified commerce" was heard as "is that the readers?", which invited a front-desk demand we couldn't show live, and the in-store half of the business stayed with Global Payments.

changes.current_line: Proven ROI, backed by an independent economic impact study.
changes.change: For the controller or finance approver, don't lead with the independent study. Offer a takeaway spreadsheet built from their own failed renewals: "Here's the revenue you can recover from your own failed renewals. Take it, check it, and set it against what switching costs you." Get it to finance before the contract reaches them.
changes.why: The contract sat with the controller for two weeks and was signed four days after the own-data session, in which the previously silent controller asked for the spreadsheet. He had asked about termination fees twice, so the cost of switching was clearly on his mind.
